content:
If you're a power user of Apple Watch apps who participated in the beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The related updates are being pushed via the App Store, with the update notes stating: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27, and includes no new features."

Apple notified developers this week that the process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and all other new operating systems) is expected to roll out to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being pushed out well in advance.

Apple said that due to issues with the arm64 slice of some watchOS apps, this handling is required. It appears they are automatically re-processing and re-packaging the apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue running without developers needing to take any action.
